quiz_overview.conditions: Sin diccionario. Sin notas. Sin compañero. Audio de Listening reproducido 2 veces durante el cuestionario.

reading_text.title: The Morning Protocol at The Diesel Workshop
reading_text.text: Every morning, Carlos Mendoza inspects The Diesel Workshop. First, he checks the three service bays. He looks at the floor — no spills, no tools on the floor. Then he checks the toolboxes. All tools must be in the right place. Next, he inspects the PPE area. Gloves and safety goggles must be available. Finally, he checks the fire extinguisher near the bay door. When everything is ready, he tells the team: 'Bay 1 is ready. Bay 2 is ready. Bay 3 is ready.' The workshop is safe. The day can start.
grammar_structures_present: There is/are (implied — no spills, no tools)

listening_script.title: Bay 1 Readiness Check
listening_script.setting: The Diesel Workshop — Bay 1 — Monday 7:15 AM

script.speaker: Santiago
script.line: Carlos, Bay 1 is ready. I checked the floor jack — no leaks.

script.speaker: Carlos

script.speaker: Santiago

script.speaker: Carlos

script.speaker: Santiago

script.speaker: Carlos

script.speaker: Carlos

sections.title: Section 2 — Key Vocabulary
sections.instructions: Choose the correct word or answer for each question. Write only the letter.
sections.design_note: Items cover terms NOT primarily tested in Cuestionario No 1: spill, work order, preventive maintenance, specialist, hazard.

items.question: Santiago found liquid on the floor near Bay 2. He said: 'There is a ___ near the bay door.'
Before a repair, Valentina fills in a document with the vehicle, the problem, and the required service. This document is called a ___.
Which of these is a TYPE of maintenance?
Carlos Mendoza is a diesel ___. He knows how to repair and maintain diesel engines.
Which word does NOT belong in the 'Tools & Equipment' category?
items.justification: wrench and socket are Tools & Equipment. hazard belongs to Safety.

sections.title: Section 3 — Grammar Structures
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option (a, b, or c) to complete each sentence or identify the error. Write only the letter.

items.question: Which sentence is a correct imperative instruction?

options.a: Checks the floor jack before starting.
options.b: Check the floor jack before starting.
options.c: You check the floor jack before starting.

items.explanation: Imperative = base form verb, no subject. Option a adds -s (wrong). Option c has subject 'you' (not imperative).

items.question: Complete the safety instruction: '___ tools on the floor.'
items.explanation: Don't + base form = correct negative imperative. 'Not leave' is incomplete. 'Don't leaving' is grammatically incorrect.

items.question: Complete the observation: '___ a spill near the bay door.'
items.explanation: 'A spill' is singular → There IS. 'There are' = plural. 'Is there' = question form.

items.question: Which sentence is correct?

options.a: There is three wrenches on the workbench.
options.b: There are three wrenches on the workbench.
options.c: There have three wrenches on the workbench.

items.explanation: 'Three wrenches' is plural → There ARE. 'There is' = singular only. 'There have' does not exist in English.

items.question: The floor jack is ___ Bay 1. (It is beside Bay 1, not inside it.)
items.explanation: 'Next to' = beside, adjacent. 'In' = inside. 'Under' = below. The floor jack is next to (beside) the bay, not inside it.

sections.title: Section 4 — Listening Comprehension
sections.instructions: You will listen to a conversation at The Diesel Workshop. The audio plays TWO times. First: listen for the general situation. Second: listen for specific details. Then answer the 5 questions. No script. No extra audio.
sections.audio_ref: Bay 1 Readiness Check — Santiago Ríos + Carlos Mendoza

items.question: Who is reporting to Carlos Mendoza?
What does Santiago check first, according to his report?
items.audio_ref_line: Carlos, Bay 1 is ready. I checked the floor jack — no leaks.

items.question: Where are the gloves?
Where are the goggles?
Is there a spill in Bay 1?
items.audio_ref_line: No. The floor is clean. No spills.

sections.title: Section 5 — Communicative Functions
sections.instructions: Read each situation. Choose the correct communicative function (a, b, or c).

items.scenario: Carlos says to Santiago: 'Check the floor jack before starting. Don't leave tools on the floor.'
items.question: What communicative function is Carlos using?
items.explanation: Imperative verbs (Check, Don't leave) directed at a colleague = F1 — Giving instructions.

items.scenario: Santiago says to his colleague: 'Can I have the torque wrench, please? I need it for Bay 2.'
items.question: What communicative function is Santiago using?
items.explanation: 'Can I have the ___?' and 'I need the ___' are F2 formulas for requesting tools or help.

items.scenario: Valentina tells Carlos: 'There is a spill near the bay door. The fire extinguisher is next to the workbench.'
items.question: What communicative function is Valentina using?
items.explanation: 'There is a spill near...' and 'The ___ is next to...' are F3 structures for describing bay conditions.

items.scenario: Santiago tells Carlos: 'Bay 2 is ready. The floor jack is OK — no leaks. All tools are in the right place.'
items.question: What communicative function is Santiago using?
items.explanation: Reporting bay status + technical conditions to the lead technician = F4 — Reporting to supervisor.

items.scenario: Carlos gives Santiago an instruction. Santiago responds: 'Understood. I'll do it now.'
items.question: What communicative function is Santiago using?
items.explanation: 'Understood.' and 'I'll do it now.' are F5 formulas for confirming comprehension of an instruction.

bloom_distribution.note: 25 items: 10 × L1 + 14 × L2 + 1 × L3. Consistent with A1.1 knowledge assessment.

distractors_rationale.note: All distractors are plausible within the workshop universe. None are absurd. Distractors are drawn from Toolbelt terms in wrong categories or grammatically adjacent structures.
examples: Item 3: 'hard hat' is a real PPE item but not in the text — plausible distractor.
Item 10: 'wrench' and 'socket' are genuine Tools & Equipment — students must know hazard belongs to Safety.
Item 13: 'Is there' is grammatically real (question form) but wrong for a statement context.
Item 22: F1 is a plausible distractor because imperatives ARE in the sentence — but the function is requesting, not giving instructions.
